crates/veilvoice-core/tests/hostile_audio.rs

veilvoice-core · 353 lines · read the source

What this file contains What calls what Items

The engine against input that is not well-behaved audio.

A realistic use of VeilVoice is "someone sent me a recording and I want to veil it before passing it on", so the input file is not necessarily friendly. A 32-bit-float WAV can legally contain NaN and infinity, and symphonia decodes those faithfully rather than sanitising them.

That matters more than it might sound, because the engine keeps persistent state: the accent neutraliser's long-term spectrum is an exponential moving average, so a single non-finite sample folded into it never washes out. The audit found exactly that — one NaN, and every output sample for the rest of the session was NaN, silently.
